title: The auth backend project
idea: The auth backend is a Node service that registers users, verifies their email, logs them in with tokens, and lets them reset a forgotten password.
points: The stack is Node.js, Express 5, MongoDB with Mongoose, JSON Web Tokens and Nodemailer.
It has no front end, so you test every route with an API client.
Each lesson adds one piece and shows only what it adds.
Chapter 6 explained authentication; here you build a full service.

hero.title: One user's journey through the service

steps.caption: A visitor registers. The client sends a username, email and password to the API.
The API hashes the password and saves the user in MongoDB. The account starts unverified.
It also emails a verification link. Opening that link proves the address is real.
The user opens the link. The API marks the account verified.
Now the user logs in with their password.
The API checks the password and replies with two cookies: an access token and a refresh token.
Later requests carry the access token, so the API knows the caller without asking for the password.
The access token expires. The client trades the refresh token for a new one and stays logged in.

takeaway: Build one service: register, verify, log in, stay logged in, recover.

starters: Why does the API send a verification email?
Why use two tokens instead of one?
Why test with an API client and not a front end?
